extraction.name: XTREME-S
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating universal cross-lingual speech representations across 102 languages, covering four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation, and retrieval. It aims to simplify multilingual speech representation evaluation and includes seven downstream tasks across multiple domains.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: XTREME-S is a benchmark assembled from multiple existing evaluation datasets for multilingual speech tasks, and distributed via the HuggingFace platform.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The benchmark uses speech datasets including Fleurs, MLS, and VoxPopuli across 102 languages and multiple task families.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The paper does not describe a human labeling workflow in detail, but it notes that FLEURS was created by collecting speech recordings for predefined sentences, with between one and three recordings per sentence (2.3 on average), and that MINDS-14 contains 14 intents extracted from the e-banking domain.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: For FLEURS, between one and three recordings per sentence, 2.3 on average.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Performance disparities exist across language and geographic groups, with substantially better results on Western European languages than on Sub-Saharan African and South Asian languages, partly due to more unlabeled data being available for Western European languages.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark has open public test sets rather than hidden ones, relying on practitioners to use dev sets properly and on prediction submission checks. The paper also notes remaining gaps in performance across language families/groups, indicating limitations in generalization and equity across languages.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to improve speech technology access across the world's languages, especially for under-represented language speakers, to give them an equal voice online and help share their content and culture beyond their language communities.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Language and geography-related group information are discussed, including under-represented languages, geographical groups, and language families.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is an evaluation benchmark for multilingual speech representation learning across recognition, translation, classification, and retrieval. Usage guidelines specify using dev sets for hyperparameter tuning, reporting test performance, allowing additional unlabeled data for pre-training/self-training, restricting fine-tuning supervision by task, and requiring reproducibility and explicit reporting of external data and language models.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Use of additional unlabeled speech/text data and possible augmentation such as TTS-augmented data or augmenting training sets from MT data is allowed for benchmark submissions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Possible filtering of large unlabeled text datasets to adapt them to each task and domain is discussed.

name.evidence: We introduce XTREME-S, a new benchmark to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations in many languages.

description.evidence: XTREME-S covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval. Covering 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains and 4 task families, XTREME-S aims to simplify multilingual speech representation evaluation

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: XTREME-S is meant to be a more exhaustive, thorough and complete evaluation of learned speech representations. It covers 102 diverse languages spanning more than 10 language families and includes four different task families: recognition, translation, classification and retrieval.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: “We do encourage submissions that also use different unlabeled speech... or using TTS-augmented data etc” and “The TTS systems used to potentially augment the training set from the MT data should be reproducible.”

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: “We hope the community can also develop smarter ways to adapt these very large unlabeled text datasets to each particular task and domain through filtering methods.”
